text: Saylor Says BIP-110 Fork Has Just 0.15% of Bitcoin Hashpower Michael Saylor said about 99.85% of Bitcoin's hashpower remained on the main chain after the BIP-110 fork, while the minority branch mined only two blocks and fell more than 80 blocks behind. He estimated the BIP-110 chain has roughly 0.15% of network hashpower and, at its current pace, could take around 25 years to reach its first difficulty adjustment. The fork follows BIP-110's attempt to temporarily restrict non-financial data embedded in Bitcoin transactions. — link

text: Highlight Clip Michael Saylor: We Sold Bitcoin to Prove It Wouldn't Crash the Market Michael Saylor: We Sold Bitcoin to Prove It Wouldn't Crash the Market Strategy founder Michael Saylor said in an August 6 interview with The Diary Of A CEO that the market believed Strategy could not sell Bitcoin because doing so might cause BTC to crash, leaving the company trapped in a "doom loop" of repeatedly selling equity to pay dividends. To break that narrative, Strategy sold Bitcoin when BTC was trading at around $59,000 to $60,000, and the price instead moved higher. Saylor said the company's break-even point is about 3.2%, meaning that if Bitcoin appreciates by that amount, Strategy can sell part of its BTC to pay dividends without continuing to sell equity. — link

text: MARA Pledges 18,750 BTC to Secure $600 Million in New Loans for Energy and AI Infrastructure Expansion According to The Energy Mag, MARA completed two loans with Coinbase Credit and Two Prime Lending on Aug. 4, pledging 18,750 BTC worth about $1.2 billion to secure $600 million new funding. The facilities have a principal of $750 million, including a $450 million Coinbase loan refinancing an existing $150 million credit line, resulting in $300 million of new funding from Coinbase, while Two Prime provided $300 million. The Coinbase facility carries an interest rate of about 7.5%, while the Two Prime loan has a fixed rate of 7.65%, with both maturing in 2028. MARA said the proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, including energy asset acquisitions and expansion of Bitcoin mining, AI and high-performance computing infrastructure. — link

text: BIP-110 Minority Fork Falls 18 Blocks Behind Bitcoin Main Chain A minority fork backed by BIP-110 supporters emerged after Bitcoin block height 961,632. The BIP-110-supporting pool Roughnecks had produced only blocks 961,632 and 961,633, while the Bitcoin chain had advanced to block 961,651, putting it 18 blocks ahead. The split coincided with Bitcoin's mining difficulty adjusting to 127.48 T. Because the BIP-110 chain has far less hash power while operating at the same difficulty, its block production has slowed. BIP-110 supporter Matthew Kratter acknowledged that the minority chain would require a "massive change" to overtake the main chain, while some supporters have begun discussing a switch to a proof-of-work algorithm. — link
